pr_title: random: Add syscalls for random subsystem
pr_body:
Create syscalls to make possible using random APIs from user mode
threads. These APIs can have different implementations, like using
entropy driver or Xoroshiro128. Some of these implementations also have
some globals to preserve state between calls.

Make it run entire in user space would require user adding these globals
to their memeory domains and/or grant access to entropy device. Syscalls
simplify its usage.

Signed-off-by: Flavio Ceolin <flavio.ceolin@intel.com>

Fixes #26499
pr_comments:
A little reasoning as to why I prefer this over the #25890 solution.

1. This better protects the DBRG state. The internal state of the DBRG needs to be protected the same as a private or encryption key. Making these syscalls allows the state to be kept entirely in kernel.
2. With hardware crypto, or something like TF-M, the state will need to be kept on the secure side, and we would need syscalls to access it anyway.
Could we get this merged soon, I would need this support in other PRs.

This happens more and more often, for more and more people and cases. Turns out, Zephyr's test runner is designed for hanging, then timing out: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/26209 . And when reported, the best response received is that it "had been such for years".

> can you restart CI 

Just close/reopen, that's the modern version of the older "recheck" trick. (I did that a few hours ago. As you can see, it still fails. Previously are suspected non-reliable hardware used for tests. Now I suspect that just test runner has erratic behavior, and it just gets exposed.)

> > just some some error cause by timeout.
> 
> This happens more and more often, for more and more people and cases. Turns out, Zephyr's test runner is designed for hanging, then timing out: #26209 . And when reported, the best response received is that it "had been such for years".

The testing framework is currently undergoing some greater verification and update. You are right that some problems were not tackled for too long but it was not because of bad will of the framework maintainers but due to the nature of an opensource project. I believe we were unaware of many problems in the design. We are now consolidating our efforts to improve the performance of the framework. 
One of the issues with timeout behavior is being addressed by #26223. We are open to changes and highly value all the input that can lead to an improvement of the framework, so please don't hesitate to raise more issues so we can be aware of pitfalls that are certainly still in the framework.

issue_context.title: usermode: random: backport random syscall
issue_context.body: Random numbers cannot easily be generate from usermode. Though there is syscall for the entropy driver, an user thread  must give access to the used driver before use it, what is not clear at all. Also it fix an inconsistency in the random subsystem where depending the backend you are using it works in usermode.

review_comments: why are you taking the header include out of kernel_includes?
nevermind, I looked at the commit message where it is described... I suspect you ran into this when adding the ctrdbg stuff... ;-)
nope, the initial patch had this problem. rand32.h now includes an auto-generated file that is not available for unit tests.
would you want to make copies of the parameters and perform parameter checks only on the copies using z_user_from_copy() api? Seems like this approach is more safer and avoids the TOCTOU attacks.

Are you suggesting making a copy of the value in dst? How does this value get changed between the Z_SYSCALL_MEMORY_WRITE() and z_impl_sys_rand_get()? Now if it was a pointer to a pointer then there might be a problem but the initial call to is the memory area to validate.
